r-james.name: James Fitchett
r-james.owns: Keeping both teams aligned. Keeping the prototype and trailer on track. Leads the business team, and supports Gray on technical work.
r-james.deliverables: Business plan doc shell (started Nov 4). Hub overview deck to the drive. Lab research. Round robin on every storyboard. Dec 3 pitch.
r-james.outlook: Keeps both teams pointed at the same game, and the business plan tied to what design is building.

r-gray.name: Gray Siegler
r-gray.owns: Engine and technical decisions. The build.
r-gray.deliverables: Initial playable build by end of November. Expand the 4 modes to about 10 bullets each, with Julia.

r-julia.name: Julia Schnittger
r-julia.deliverables: Expand the 4 modes with Gray. Creative direction for the prototype and trailer.

r-eleazar.name: Eleazar Reiner
r-eleazar.owns: Scenarios, levels, and the decision-tree mechanic.
r-eleazar.deliverables: More ideas for modes beyond the Hub. Scenario drafts for the prototype.
r-eleazar.outlook: Moves to the business team after this phase. Brings deep design context and keeps working closely with the design team.

r-ashrita.name: Ashrita Sagar
r-ashrita.owns: Art direction, world and environment art.
r-ashrita.deliverables: Art for the prototype and trailer.

r-mark.name: Mark Sangkharat
r-mark.deliverables: Marketable trailer. Playtest plan and sessions.

r-colin.name: Colin Larkin
r-colin.deliverables: Comparable pricing scan of 8 to 10 games. Revenue model comparison. Rough cost estimates with Gray. Revenue and impact model by Nov 12.

r-henry.name: Henry Carey
r-henry.deliverables: Competitor scan of SDG and impact games. TAM and SAM estimate. Partner shortlist. SDG competition requirements and deadlines.

d-proto.name: Playable prototype
d-proto.what: A first-pass playable build of the Hub. Proposed scope: one real place, a few AI residents, one live-style crisis, and the your-call-vs-reality screen.
d-proto.doneLooks: Someone outside the team can play a full loop (build, talk, crisis, compare) in about 10 minutes without help.
d-proto.why: Proves the Hub works and is fun. Everything else, from the trailer to the pitch, leans on it.

d-trailer.name: Marketable trailer
d-trailer.what: A 60 to 90 second trailer that sells the Hub: a real place, a real crisis, residents who talk back, friends sending aid.
d-trailer.doneLooks: After one watch, a stranger can say what the game is and why it matters.
d-trailer.why: How people outside the team first understand the game. It sells the vision in under two minutes.

d-plan.name: Business plan
d-plan.what: Revenue and impact model, market size, competitors, partners, costs, and how we reach players.
d-plan.doneLooks: A document the advisors can read in 15 minutes, ready to showcase at the last December class.
d-plan.why: It's the backbone. It turns the game into a venture judges, partners and funders can back, and it feeds the Hult and SDG competitions and any funding we apply for.

d-pitch.name: Dec 3 presentation
d-pitch.what: One unified pitch for the sponsors and the dean.
d-pitch.doneLooks: A clear story in under 5 minutes: our genre, the Hub, why it matters.
d-pitch.why: Where the plan, prototype and trailer come together in one story for the advisors and the dean.

t12.name: Engine choice and AI resident spike

h01.statement: elicit awareness on the UN 17 SDGs?

h04.statement: build a virtual gaming ecosystem that addresses the lack of social change relative to the 17 SDGs?
h04.notes: Names the solution (a game). The 5 A's say a problem framing shouldn't.

h05.statement: build a game that helps solve the UN 17 SDGs?

h08.statement: build something people love and want to use?

h09.statement: make players feel a real crisis without exploiting the people living it?

h10.statement: turn player decisions into insight real partners can use?

h11.statement: make a single-player world feel alive with AI residents?

h12.statement: make coming back every day feel like caring, not a chore?

f01.text: Players will care about a real place and people they get to know, and come back to protect them. Real-world events give a reason to log in that fictional games don't have.

f02.text: Daily-login loops work even without deep enjoyment (the team's Clash of Clans experience). Citizen-science games drew millions: Sea Hero Quest about 4.3 million players, Borderlands Science about 4.5 million.

f03.text: Real crises may feel heavy or exploitative. Teen players may see it as homework.

f04.text: Playtest the Hub loop with each persona. Measure return rate and how players describe it.

f05.text: A small team can ship a first playable Hub this semester by scoping to one place, a few residents and template-based crises.

f06.text: Small, low-energy AI models can run conversational characters. Crisis templates scaled per event mean we don't hand-write every scenario.

f07.text: Limited game-dev experience. AI cost and safety. Screening real-time events needs people.

f08.text: Engine choice and an AI resident spike by mid-November.

f09.text: Free solo play with paid global play, cosmetics and school editions can fund the game. The mission opens grants and competitions.

f10.text: Business research in progress: pricing scan, revenue model and competitor scan due Nov 12. Godus, a key reference, was Kickstarter-funded.

f11.text: Monetizing an educational game without feeling exploitative. School sales cycles are slow.

f12.text: Revenue and impact model by Nov 12. Price-sensitivity questions in playtests.

f13.text: Awareness turns into action through co-op aid, Lab insight handed to NGOs, the Hall of Best Decisions, and a share of profits to real SDG work.

f14.text: Foldit and Borderlands Science show player work can produce published science.

f15.text: AI and data centers carry an energy cost that cuts against some goals. Political content could harm the communities we depict.

f16.text: Pick a small model and estimate energy per session. Consult a partner NGO on one depicted crisis.

q01.question: Where's our line on politics? Renamed but recognizable is the current lean.
q01.context: Store policies, school partners, VT and Hult judges, sponsors, and the safety of the communities we depict.

q02.question: One community per player, or several? Can communities be lost or taken?
q02.context: Raised in James's Hub storyboard, Nov 5.

q03.question: AI can be wrong or biased about real events. Who screens it, and how fast?
q03.context: Round robin critique, Nov 5. Rebuttal: AI gathers, a person screens before release.

q04.question: Simulated solutions can look reductive or even harmful. Do we frame the game as a brainstorm, not the final word?

q05.question: How do non-physical goals like education and equality show up in the Hub?
q05.context: City-builder critique, Nov 5: buildings are easy, education is not.

q06.question: Does the daily hook pull attention away from deeper learning?

q07.question: Which research or NGO partner would actually use Lab data?
q07.context: Without a partner the Lab's data has no home.

q08.question: Does the story inform the game, or the game inform the story?
q08.context: No consensus on Nov 5. Exploring both for now.

q09.question: What genre do we say we are to outsiders like the dean?
q09.context: Needed for the Dec 3 presentation to the advisors and the dean.

q10.question: PC first: does it fit teen and casual players who mostly play on phones?

q11.question: 16 games or 17? Is SDG 17 the game itself?
q11.context: Nov 5: a teammate framed the 17th goal as the game itself.

p-teen.name: Jayden, the competitive teen
p-teen.who: High schooler who plays Fortnite and Clash with friends after school. Picks games his group is already playing.
p-teen.wants: Competition, rank, playing with friends, quick wins, things to show off.
p-teen.frustrations: Anything that feels like homework. Slow starts. Lecturing.
p-teen.quote: If my friends aren't on it, I'm not on it.

p-college.name: Priya, the campus changemaker
p-college.segment: 19 to 23, green club or service org
p-college.who: College student who heard about 17SG through an academic or sustainability club. Already cares about the goals.
p-college.wants: To feel her time actually helps. Real outcomes, credit, something to tell her club about.
p-college.frustrations: Slacktivism. Games that trivialize real suffering.
p-college.quote: Show me it actually did something.

p-casual.name: Linda, the casual player
p-casual.who: Plays Candy Crush-style games in short breaks. Stumbled onto 17SG through a friend or the news.
p-casual.wants: Relaxing, short sessions, characters she can care about, a feeling of doing good.
p-casual.frustrations: Complex controls, competitive pressure, violent content.
p-casual.quote: I just like checking in on my little town.

p-sim.name: Sam, the strategy sim fan
p-sim.segment: 20 to 35, PC strategy and city builders
p-sim.who: Plays Cities: Skylines, Tropico and Civilization. Loves systems, trade-offs and optimizing.
p-sim.wants: Depth, real cause and effect, a high skill ceiling, things that matter long term.
p-sim.frustrations: Shallow mechanics, obvious right answers, mobile-style monetization.
p-sim.quote: Let me see what breaks if I push it.

p-whale.name: Marcus, the power user
p-whale.segment: 22 to 40, plays daily, spends the most
p-whale.who: The top slice of players who log in every day and spend on cosmetics and boosts. Wants status.
p-whale.wants: High stakes, exclusivity, leaderboards, recognition like the Hall of Best Decisions.
p-whale.frustrations: Running out of meaningful things to do. Pay-to-win from others.
p-whale.quote: Give me the hardest thing you've got.

p-diaspora.name: Amina, the player with a stake
p-diaspora.segment: 18 to 30, family tied to a crisis region
p-diaspora.who: Has family in a region the game depicts. Will judge whether we tell that story with care.
p-diaspora.wants: Accuracy, dignity, a way to make friends understand what her family lives through.
p-diaspora.frustrations: Stereotypes, getting the politics wrong, suffering used as spectacle.
p-diaspora.quote: If you're going to show my home, get it right.

p-creator.name: Dev, the streamer
p-creator.segment: 18 to 30, streams on Twitch or YouTube
p-creator.who: Content creator who needs dramatic, shareable moments and audience participation.
p-creator.wants: Big moments, chat interaction, controversy that drives views, new content often.
p-creator.frustrations: Long stretches with nothing happening. Content that gets videos demonetized.
p-creator.quote: Chat, do we evacuate or sandbag?

p-teacher.name: Ms. Alvarez, the civics teacher
p-teacher.who: Looking for something students will actually engage with that covers current events and the SDGs.
p-teacher.wants: Accuracy, a class mode, controls over content, something that fits her lesson plan.
p-teacher.frustrations: Unscreened AI chat, political blowback from parents, setup time.
p-teacher.quote: Can I run this in a 50-minute period?

p-parent.name: Rob, the parent
p-parent.segment: Parent of a 12 to 16 year old
p-parent.who: Decides what his kid can play and spend on.
p-parent.wants: Safety, no open chat with strangers, clear spending limits, some educational value.
p-parent.frustrations: AI chatbots talking to his kid unsupervised. Loot-box style spending.
p-parent.quote: Who exactly is my kid talking to?

p-ngo.name: Grace, the NGO program lead
p-ngo.who: Runs programs and outreach. Could review Lab solutions and award the Hall of Best Decisions.
p-ngo.wants: Awareness for her cause, usable insight, a younger audience, no reputational risk.
p-ngo.frustrations: Oversimplified portrayals of the people she serves. Extra work with no payoff.
p-ngo.quote: What do I get from this, and what could go wrong?

p-researcher.name: Dr. Chen, the researcher
p-researcher.who: Has a problem where human pattern-spotting beats computers and needs many people to help.
p-researcher.wants: Clean, checked data at scale, players who stay engaged, credit handled properly.
p-researcher.frustrations: Noisy data, games that change the task in ways that ruin it.
p-researcher.quote: I need ten thousand careful eyes.

s-team.name: 17SG team
s-team.interest: A great grade, a working prototype, trailer and business plan, something worth continuing.
s-team.need: Time, ownership, alignment on the Hub.

s-sponsors.name: Advisors: Prof. Kevin Jones and Dr. Mike Kretser
s-sponsors.interest: A strong Hult-style concept, real learning, a clear pitch by Dec 3. They advise both teams.

s-dean.name: The dean
s-dean.interest: IncUB8 was her idea. Wants to see what the teams have built.
s-dean.need: A crisp story about what we are and why it matters.

s-vt.name: Virginia Tech (incubator, Kickstart program)
s-vt.interest: Student ventures that reflect well on VT.

s-comps.name: Hult Prize and SDG competitions
s-comps.interest: Ventures with real SDG impact and a viable model.
s-comps.need: Prize money, visibility, deadlines to work toward.

s-players.name: Players (see Personas)
s-players.interest: Fun, friends, status, feeling they matter.
s-players.need: Time, word of mouth, spending, feedback in playtests.

s-teachers.name: Teachers and schools
s-teachers.interest: Engaging, accurate material that fits the curriculum.

s-clubs.name: University clubs and student orgs
s-clubs.interest: Ways to act on the goals together.

s-ngos.name: Humanitarian and climate NGOs
s-ngos.interest: Awareness, younger supporters, insight, no reputational risk.
s-ngos.need: Accuracy checks, Lab problems, judges for the Hall of Best Decisions.

s-un.name: UN SDG bodies and SDG game networks
s-un.need: Credibility, endorsement, possible use of SDG branding.

s-research.name: Research labs and citizen-science groups
s-research.interest: Large volumes of checked human data.
s-research.need: Real problems for the Lab science track.

s-depicted.name: People living through the crises we depict
s-depicted.interest: Being shown with dignity and accuracy, and real help.
s-depicted.need: Their stories told right. We should consult, not assume.

s-diaspora.name: Diaspora communities
s-diaspora.interest: How their home regions are portrayed.
s-diaspora.need: Feedback and trust. Can be our loudest critics or champions.

s-govts.name: Governments of depicted regions
s-govts.interest: How they are portrayed. Some may react strongly.
s-govts.need: Nothing directly. A risk to manage.

s-privacy.name: Privacy and child-safety rules (COPPA, GDPR)
s-privacy.interest: How we handle minors' data and AI chat logs.

s-ratings.name: Age-rating boards (ESRB, PEGI)
s-ratings.interest: Violence, language, user interaction, in-game purchases.
s-ratings.need: A rating that fits our audience.

s-stores.name: Stores (Steam, Epic, app stores)
s-stores.interest: Content and AI policies, revenue share.

s-engine.name: Game engine provider
s-engine.need: The tools to build the prototype.

s-ai.name: AI model providers
s-ai.need: Affordable, small models for AI residents.

s-cloud.name: Cloud and data-center hosts
s-cloud.need: Servers, with an energy footprint that fits our values.

s-creators.name: Streamers, press and creators
s-creators.need: Coverage that drives players to us.

s-backers.name: Crowdfunding backers and investors
s-backers.interest: A game they believe in, a return or reward.

s-sponsorbrands.name: Sponsors and brands
s-sponsorbrands.interest: Association with doing good, reach to young players.
s-sponsorbrands.need: Sponsored school events, funding. Watch the politics fit.

s-sme.name: Subject-matter experts and fact-checkers
s-sme.interest: Accuracy on crises, policy and science.
s-sme.need: Review of crisis templates and Lab problems.

s-wellbeing.name: Mental health and crisis-support organizations
s-wellbeing.interest: Players exposed to heavy real-world content.
s-wellbeing.need: Guidance on content warnings and support links.

s-localadvisors.name: Local cultural advisors and translators
s-localadvisors.interest: Places portrayed in their own terms.
s-localadvisors.need: Review of names, language and cultural detail.

s-access.name: Accessibility advocates and disabled players
s-access.interest: Being able to play: controls, captions, color, reading load.

s-trust.name: Trust and safety reviewers
s-trust.interest: Safe AI conversations and player chat.
s-trust.need: Rules and review for AI residents and multiplayer.

s-competitors.name: Comparable and competing games
s-competitors.interest: The same players and the same SDG-education niche.
s-competitors.need: Lessons on what works and where they fall short.
